title: AIA, Allianz Retire+ join forces on retirement engagement
full_text:
Allianz Retire+ and AIA Australia are partnering to target financial advisers and help them realise the value of longevity and retirement income products.
The partnership will see AIA and Allianz Retire+ partner to bring the insurers’s abilities together and prepare clients for retirement through both a wellbeing and a guaranteed income approach.
Both insurers point that 2.8 million Australians who are set to retire in the next decade, while research from the Super Members Council (SMC) found that 75 per cent of pre -retirees find the range of super retirement products confusing, and that retirement system complexity could cost a typical retiree up to $136,000 over the course of retirement.
AIA flagged its expertise in health and wellbeing and says it wants to keep Australians healthier during their working lives, notably through its ‘AIA Vitality program’.
“We know that people are currently living longer, but they’re not necessarily spending their later years in good health; and financial security plays a big part in someone’s overall wellbeing,” pointed Damien MU, CEO of AIA Australia.
Through the partnership, clients will have access to AIA’s wellbeing program, combined with Allianz+ expertise in lifetime income, including its Allianz Guaranteed Income for Life (AGILE) product.
AGILE operates in two main stages: investment growth, followed by the ‘Lifetime Income Phase’, when clients choose to convert their investment value into guaranteed regular payments.
In terms of clients, the partnership targets superannuation funds, wealth platforms, financial advisers and retirement services.
“Allianz Retire+ is experiencing positive momentum as advisers, superannuation funds and retirees increasingly recognise the value of retirement income solutions, including Allianz Guaranteed Income for Life (AGILE).
“This reflects a broader shift in how Australians are preparing for retirement and managing longevity risk,” declared David Kane, CEO of Allianz Retire+.
The insurers aim to create a lifelong experience to navigate key moments, through a framework of Engage > Protect > Recover > Prepare > Retire.
First, AIA will incentivise clients to be healthy throughout their lives and engage in retirement early.
At the same time, Allianz Retire+’s AGILE solution allows people to start locking in a retirement income from age 50. After retirement, it is set to provide a guaranteed income for the remainder of a person’s life.
Along the journey, AIA will address issues around clients remaining active, healthy and socially connected once they have stopped working full –time.
Responding to Money Management, the insurers clarified that the partnership was not about developing a new product, but rather bringing together existing capabilities.
“It’s not a product play but a member engagement play. It is about extending the member engagement functionality of Vitality (AIA) and leveraging the AGILE (Allianz) chassis to build solutions for members types, get them engaged and thinking about retirement early.
“Our focus is now on working with super funds, advisers and other retirement providers to explore how these capabilities can support their members,” said the insurers.”
Earlier this year, Allianz Retire+ updated its AGILE solution with a product fee reduction and faster access to lifetime income, following adviser feedback.
